_what: Practice scenarios for the connector curriculum, served by crm/coach.py. Content, not code.
_rule: Every drill maps to a lesson slug that exists in this folder and practises something that lesson TEACHES. A drill testing material the curriculum never covers is a trick question, not coaching.
_authored: 2026-08-24. Authored, never generated — reviewable by the Founder, and identical between runs so two connectors practising the same rung get the same test.
_honesty: n=0 connectors. No drill may claim what 'top connectors' do, quote a success rate, or imply a benchmark. Rubrics describe what the DOCUMENTED rules require, nothing more.

01-the-intro-play.prompt: You are at a kid's game and a friend who runs a 12-truck plumbing company says 'we're drowning, phone rings all day and we miss half of it.' Make the introduction, out loud, right now.
01-the-intro-play.looks_like: Warm and specific. Names the pain in the owner's own words. Offers to connect, does not pitch yourco's product or mechanism. Ends with a clear next step they control ('can I introduce you to the Founder?').
01-the-intro-play.fails_if: They explain how the AI works, name a price, promise a result or a timeline, or say 'I'll set it up for you' — the connector's job ends at the introduction.

01-the-intro-play.prompt: The owner replies to your intro email directly and asks: 'What's this going to cost me?' Answer them.
01-the-intro-play.looks_like: Declines to quote, without sounding evasive. Redirects to the audit and to the Founder. Something like: 'I genuinely don't quote — that's the Founder's side. What I can tell you is the audit itself is free right now.'
01-the-intro-play.fails_if: Any number at all, any range, any 'probably around', or negotiating. Quoting a price is the one thing the acknowledgement on lesson 01 explicitly forbids.

02-who-to-flag.prompt: Rank these three and say why: (a) a 40-person SaaS company wanting to 'add AI to the product', (b) a 6-person HVAC shop where the owner books every job from his truck, (c) a solo consultant who loves tinkering with no-code tools.
02-who-to-flag.looks_like: b first — owner-operated, misses inbound, high job value, wants it handled. a is out: wrong shape, not owner-felt pain, wants product AI not operations. c is out: DIY tinkerer, explicitly a bad fit in the lesson.
02-who-to-flag.fails_if: Picks the biggest company because it sounds more impressive, or fails to name WHY the tinkerer is a bad fit.

02-who-to-flag.prompt: Say the one qualifying question from the lesson, word for word.
02-who-to-flag.looks_like: 'Which of the business owners you know is losing business because they can't get to the phone?'
02-who-to-flag.fails_if: A generic 'do you need AI?' or 'are you interested in automation?' — the lesson's whole point is that the question names a symptom the owner already feels.

05-the-rules-of-the-road.prompt: A prospect you referred asks you to sit in on the proposal call and 'help them decide'. What do you do?
05-the-rules-of-the-road.looks_like: Declines the advisory role, stays in the relationship. Does not negotiate, interpret terms, or advocate on price. Hands it to the Founder and offers to stay available socially.
05-the-rules-of-the-road.fails_if: Agrees to 'just help them understand it' — that is negotiating on yourco's behalf, which the acknowledgement forbids regardless of intent.

14-submitting-contacts.prompt: You want to submit a name as a Sourcer rather than make the intro yourself. Give me the two things you must include, and say why the second one exists.
14-submitting-contacts.looks_like: How you know them, and their consent answer. The consent answer exists because on a Sourcer submission YOURCO becomes the caller — so TCPA/FTSA/CAN-SPAM attach to yourco, not to the connector.
14-submitting-contacts.fails_if: Treats the consent question as paperwork, or cannot say that the legal exposure moves to yourco when yourco makes the approach.
